title: Impact of alphabet length B
question: How do convergence speed, overall step accuracy, and wrap-around accuracy (`splits.id.wrap_around_accuracy` in `eval.jsonl`, measuring `x_k == s_{B-1} -> s_0`) scale as the in-context alphabet size B grows from 2 up to 240, both when the symbol pool is restricted to B symbols (noting small-universe train/eval overlap at tiny B and L) and when drawn from the full 240-byte pool? (Note: at the B = 2 lower endpoint, [a, b] and [b, a] define the same cyclic swap a <-> b, testing static memorisation on a 2-symbol pool or unordered 2-symbol partner lookup on the 240-byte pool; order-sensitive lookup starts at B = 3.)
